engineering_constraints.description: Pyrolysis temperature: 500°C under N₂ atmosphere (80 mL/min) for 120 min
Silicate modification: Na₂SiO₃·9H₂O mixed with biomass at mass ratios 3:1, 2:1, 1:1 before pyrolysis
Production cost: ~0.67 USD/kg (raw), ~1.44 USD/kg (Si-modified) at lab scale; mass production reduces cost

design_translation.idea: Use agricultural waste (oiltea camellia shell, walnut shell, rice straw) as feedstock for biochar production via pyrolysis at 500°C, with silicate modification to enhance heavy metal adsorption capacity
examples: Silicate-modified oiltea camellia shell biochar for Cd removal (211 mg/g)
Walnut shell biochar for tetracycline removal
Rice straw biochar with high silica content for enhanced Cd adsorption
design_translation.applicability: Heavy metal (Cd, Pb, Cu, As) and organic pollutant (tetracycline) removal from wastewater; soil remediation

knowledge_gaps: Long-term stability and regeneration cycles need more data
Competitive adsorption in multi-metal systems not fully characterized
Scale-up from lab to industrial production not yet demonstrated

narrative.text: Biochar is a carbonaceous material pyrolyzed from biomass under oxygen-limited conditions. Its adsorption capacity depends on feedstock type, pyrolysis temperature, and surface modification. Silicate modification during pyrolysis creates fine particles (quartz, silicate, C-Si mixtures) on biochar surface, increasing SSA by 45-112% and exposing more adsorption sites for heavy metals.
